messages.author: cefd17aea0d7c422
messages.subject: different facet widths
parts:
Dear All,

I have a very specific question about ggplot2. I’d like to plot frequencies in a stacked bar chart (please find data, R file and plot attached). If all the vertical facets are scaled the same with frequencies ranging from 0 to 600, some facets with less counts don’t look nice. Is there a way to shrink facets with less counts? Specifying scales = "free" and space = "free" obviously didn’t work.

Best wishes

Andreas Meid

messages.author: 0c39e60ddb38622b
messages.subject: Re: different facet widths
parts:
Hi:

You won't be able to resize panels in facet_grid(). Look carefully at your attached graph, say in column 2; how could you sensibly resize both panels independently and retain some sense of consistency in the display? 

There is an example in http://www.nature.com/psp/journal/v2/n10/full/psp201356a.html (see Figure 7) of how to resize facets, but it requires facet_wrap(). You would need to combine your two factors into one (e.g., via paste() or interaction()) so you'd lose the 2D structure of facet_grid(), but then you could resize the panels if you wished.

Personally, I'd leave the present display alone as the missing categories are informative and the structure allows for easy comparison, but the cited article provides an example of how to shrink panels if you want it.

Dennis
